replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
The play looks like a proof of concept. What’s the cohesion and balancing between units and factions?  Has OP played them all against each other and different ones and see how it actually performs? AI isn’t super good at “balancing” things just yet. It can test headless which is awesome and provide you a ton of data. But it’s not that great at balance. 

Granted. Maybe OP just told it “make it like World War I “game someone linked and all the balancing came from there.  But I doubt he actually played it properly to test everything on the 3 days it took Claude to make it.

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body: Yea 3 days is not enough for a good game, but this has solid bones for tweaking. I think for 3 days its a good tech demo.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
Most of these. That’s all they are. Proof of concept or tech demo. Then - USUALLY - two things tend to happen. They either try to ship it as is - Claude balanced and tested, or they realize how much systems mechanics and balance na actually requires in terms of work - and quit.

I said usually because there are some that will stick with it or use this knowledge for the next one and actually produce something worth playing.

comments.author: jss1977
comments.body:
These posts are why actually good AI assisted games and projects get branded as AI Slop. It’s great you’re having fun, but there’s no “game” here. It’s just game mechanics assembled by an algorithm based on its internal knowledge and training.

Do the work, create a design document, find an innovative gameplay loop and then use AI to help you build YOUR vision. If all you’re doing is responding to multiple choice questions, then you may as well get another AI to respond on your behalf and close the loop.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body: Most of these games have no cohesion as a game, no plot or story, no real balancing. It’s more of a “proof of concept” for “Claude did a thing”. But these while “Claude built a game in n days” are starting to get annoying.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
I have no problem with people having fun. But the whole “I built a game with Claude in n days” posts just mostly scream ai slop. The coding is good and the assets are getting better each day so it’s easy to do, but besides telling Claude to make “x”. What did the user “create” here. 

I have no problem with vibe coding. And it the game is good and fun and cohesive and well balanced then the amount of time spent on it is irrelevant. I just want to know what did the user actually do here and how much of it was all Claude ideas and planning and execution.

And again, how was the balancing done? How are the units balanced.

The more I work with Claude to build my own projects. The more I realize how stupid and at the same time confident it is in what is “fun” or balance.

And most is these people just accept the game as is and done

replies.author: PulIthEld
replies.body:
why do you care what the developer did?  why not only care about the game you actully get to play?
balancing with ai is very easy, trivial even.  ai can just run simulations of the game in extra fast mode with no rendering to test whatever

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
Balancing isn’t that easy with AI because what AI thinks is fun or balanced isn’t really fun or balanced. as I explained above. That’s my point. That’s why I care and the “developer” did. If he let Ai decide on the “fun” and the balancing - it’s usually pretty bad. If he had input himself and play tested it all then that’s a different story. I’ve spent weeks undoing the “balancing” AI has done before lol. Even with pretty explicit instructions on what I was looking for. I’ve realized it requires a lot more hand holding and manual testing than people realize. 

Yeah. I have it running 200 agents testing the game headless in no time compared to real players. But then I use that data to fine tune it myself. Because it sucks at that.
